title: Reading a Tablet Line
short: Most lines follow one pattern: a word or name, then a logogram, then a number; a word divider separates words.
trouble: Students read straight through, turning the logogram into a syllable. Find the word divider, the logogram and the number first, then read the word.

blocks.html: You now have every piece: the signs (The Five Vowel Signs to Special Signs), the spelling rules (Clusters and Empty Vowels), the logograms (Logograms) and the numbers (Aegean Numbers). Time to read a tablet line the way a specialist does.

Most lines follow one pattern: a word or name, then a logogram, then a number. A short stroke, the word divider, separates spelled words. Find the divider, the logogram and the number first; then read the word.

blocks.name: sc-tablet
blocks.cap: Step through the reading: signs, then transliteration, then English. Tap each part.

items: Find the number at the end of each entry: strokes, bars and circles.
Find the logogram right before it: a sign standing alone that says what is counted.
Find the word dividers, short upright strokes between spelled words.
Read the words sign by sign, then apply the spelling rules to find the Greek.

blocks.title: Read a line
blocks.q: Read this line, made for practice: 𐀓𐀈𐀛𐀊 𐂇 𐄒.
steps: Logogram: the sheep sign with the male mark, OVISm, rams.
Word: ku-do-ni-ja, Kydonia (modern Chania), a place.

blocks.title: Read a line
steps: Word: ti-ri-po, tripod, which matches the picture.

blocks.html: Why start from the end? Because the number and the logogram can be read even when the word cannot. If the word is a name you have never seen, you still know what and how many. Scholars read damaged tablets this way: the logogram and number often survive when part of the word is broken.

Reading straight through and turning the logogram into a syllable, as if 𐀂𐀦 𐂃 were a three-syllable word. Find the word divider, the logogram and the number first, then read the word. Check: a logogram is never joined to the signs before it; it stands alone before the number.

blocks.name: sc-tablet
blocks.cap: A harder one: Ta 641, with several entries on one line. Find each logogram and number first.

blocks.html: Real tablets are often damaged. Editors mark a break in the clay with square brackets: ke-ka-u-me-no] means the tablet breaks off after that sign. When a number is broken, you may still read the logogram and know what was counted, but not how many.

blocks.title: A Ta 641 entry
blocks.q: On Ta 641 one entry reads 𐀤𐀵 𐃢 𐄉. What is counted, and how many?
steps: Word: qe-to, the name of that kind of jar.

blocks.html: The lines in practice problems are made in the style of real tablets, with words from real Linear B texts, to give you practice; they are not copies of particular tablets.
